How to use NoteCraft on another computer
=========================================

NoteCraft is one file: NoteCraft.exe. There is nothing to install.
It runs on any 64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11 computer.
Pages are shown with Microsoft Edge WebView2, which Windows 10 and 11
already include. On a very old Windows 10 without it, NoteCraft still
works with a simpler page view; installing "WebView2 Runtime" from
Microsoft brings the full view back.

1. Copy NoteCraft.exe to the other computer
   - with a USB stick, by e-mail, or through the shared folder;
   - put it somewhere handy, for example in Documents.
   Tip: you can also keep NoteCraft.exe in the shared notes folder itself
   and start it from there on every computer.

2. Start it
   - double-click NoteCraft.exe;
   - if Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click "More info" and
     then "Run anyway" (NoteCraft is not signed by a publisher, so
     Windows asks once).

3. Choose your notes folder
   - the first time, NoteCraft asks for the folder with your notes;
   - choose the shared folder (through "Network" or its drive letter);
   - each computer remembers its own choice; to change it, click the
     folder name at the top left of the window.

4. Make it easy to find (optional)
   - right-click NoteCraft.exe, choose "Show more options",
     "Send to", "Desktop (create shortcut)";
   - or start it, right-click its icon in the taskbar and choose
     "Pin to taskbar".

Working together
   Several computers can have the same notes open. Only one of them can
   edit a page at a time; the others see who is editing it and get the
   new text as soon as it is saved. If a computer crashes while editing,
   the page is free again after about three minutes.

New version
   Replace NoteCraft.exe with the new file on each computer (close
   NoteCraft first). Your notes and settings stay as they are.
